Estimate a mean, total, proportion or ratio from a survey design

Source: R/survey.R
survey_estimate.Rd

Design-based point estimates with standard errors, confidence intervals and coefficients of variation, for the whole population or for each domain of by. A respondent outside a domain, or missing the analysis variable, counts zero in that domain and stays in the design, so the variance of a subgroup estimate reflects the whole sample design. Use it for the figures a survey report publishes (the prevalence of a behaviour by region, the mean number of drinks, a population total) with the standard errors the survey's design implies rather than those of a simple random sample.

Usage

survey_estimate(
  design,
  data,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  stat = c("mean", "total", "proportion", "ratio"),
  denominator = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  ci = c("auto", "wilson", "logit", "wald"),
  min_n = 30,
  df = Inf
)

Arguments

design

A survey_design() built on data.

data

The data frame the design was built on.

y

Character scalar, the analysis column: numeric for a mean, total or ratio; any type for a proportion (each distinct value is a category).

by

Optional character vector of domain columns; NULL (the default) estimates for the whole population.

stat

"mean", "total", "proportion" or "ratio" (of y to denominator).

denominator

For a ratio, the denominator column.

levels

For a proportion, the categories to report (default all observed).

conf_level

Numeric scalar in (0, 1), the confidence level; default 0.95.

ci

Interval method: "auto" (the default; Wilson for proportions, Wald otherwise), "wilson", "logit" or "wald". Wilson and logit apply to proportions only.

min_n

Numeric scalar, default 30: domains with fewer respondents are flagged.

df

Degrees of freedom for the interval: Inf (the default) for the normal quantile, a number for Student's t, or "design" for the design's own (PSUs less strata under linearization, replicates less one otherwise).

Value

A data frame of class c("rmbl_svy_estimate", "data.frame"), one row per domain (and category, for a proportion): the domain columns (and level), then numeric estimate, se, lower, upper, cv (coefficient of variation, percent), integer n (respondents counted) and character flag (NA when there is nothing to say). Attributes: vcov (the covariance matrix of the estimates, used by survey_compare()), stat, y, by, ci, conf_level, df, method (the variance method) and denominator.

Details

The estimates are ratios of weighted totals: a mean is \(\sum w_i y_i / \sum w_i\) over the domain, a total \(\sum w_i y_i\), a proportion the mean of the 0/1 indicator of each category, and a ratio \(\sum w_i y_i / \sum w_i x_i\) with \(x\) the denominator. Their variances come from the design: the replicate formula, or Taylor linearization of the ratio (see survey_design()).

Proportions are reported for every category of y (or those in levels), each with its own interval. The default interval for a proportion is Wilson's score interval at the modified effective sample size of SAS PROC SURVEYFREQ, the software behind Health Canada's published Canadian Substance Use Survey intervals: \(n / \mathrm{Deff}\), with the design effect taken against the simple-random-sampling variance \(p(1 - p)/(n - 1)\), scaled by \((t_{n-1} / t_{df})^2\) for the design's degrees of freedom (Korn and Graubard 1998; \(t_{df}\) is the normal quantile when the design's degrees of freedom are infinite) and capped at the \(n\) respondents behind the estimate. ci = "logit" builds the interval on the logit scale and "wald" symmetrically. Means, totals and ratios get the symmetric normal interval.

A domain with fewer than min_n respondents is flagged, not withheld: Health Canada suppresses such CSUS estimates in its data tool (denominator under 30), and the flag lets the reader do the same. Other flags say why a standard error is missing (no stratum with two PSUs, a replicate that left the domain empty, weights all zero) or that a domain has no respondents.

Errors: design not from survey_design(); data not the rows the design was built on, in the same order; y, by or denominator naming a column data does not have; a ratio without denominator; conf_level outside (0, 1); df not positive, Inf or "design", or a design with no degrees of freedom under df = "design"; a single-PSU stratum under lonely_psu = "fail".

See also

survey_design(), survey_compare()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(region = rep(c("north", "south"), each = 50),
                smoker = rbinom(100, 1, rep(c(0.2, 0.35), each = 50)),
                drinks = rpois(100, 3), w = runif(100, 50, 150))
des <- survey_design(d, weights = "w", strata = "region")
survey_estimate(des, d, "smoker", by = "region", stat = "proportion", levels = "1")
#> Survey proportion of smoker by region (linearization variance, 95% wilson interval)
#>  region level estimate      se   lower  upper    cv  n flag
#>   north     1   0.1570 0.05295 0.08093 0.2825 33.73 50   NA
#>   south     1   0.3752 0.07282 0.25036 0.5192 19.41 50   NA
survey_estimate(des, d, "drinks", stat = "mean")
#> Survey mean of drinks (linearization variance, 95% wald interval)
#>  estimate     se lower upper    cv   n flag
#>     3.088 0.1668 2.761 3.415 5.401 100   NA
survey_estimate(des, d, "drinks", by = "region", stat = "total")
#> Survey total of drinks by region (linearization variance, 95% wald interval)
#>  region estimate   se lower upper    cv  n flag
#>   north    15080 1390 12356 17805 9.218 50   NA
#>   south    13796 1109 11621 15970 8.041 50   NA

# a ratio of two totals, with Student's t on the design's degrees of freedom
d$visits <- rpois(100, 6)
survey_estimate(des, d, "drinks", stat = "ratio", denominator = "visits", df = "design")
#> Survey ratio of drinks (linearization variance, 95% wald interval)
#>  estimate      se  lower  upper    cv   n flag
#>     0.496 0.03564 0.4253 0.5667 7.185 100   NA

# a logit interval at 90 percent
survey_estimate(des, d, "smoker", stat = "proportion", levels = "1", ci = "logit",
                conf_level = 0.90)
#> Survey proportion of smoker (linearization variance, 90% logit interval)
#>  level estimate      se  lower  upper    cv   n flag
#>      1    0.261 0.04474 0.1943 0.3409 17.14 100   NA

# the design remembers its rows: a subset is refused
try(survey_estimate(des, d[-1, ], "drinks"))
#> Error : `data` must be the data frame the design was built on
